quizzes.title: Summit Theme and Objectives: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage:
India hosted a major AI gathering in 2026, and the event was presented as a turning point in how the technology is approached. Earlier global discussions on AI were described as following a Western safety-first model, which placed the management of risk ahead of other concerns. The summit signalled a different direction, an impact-first developmental paradigm in which AI is judged by the outcomes it produces for people. Under this approach, attention is directed to priority cooperation areas such as healthcare and agriculture, where AI can be put to practical use.

The gathering was planned around a guiding message of collective welfare and was organised around a set of guiding principles that shape how its work is framed. Its discussions were meant to move beyond broad global conversations and towards practical, scalable applications. Several objectives were set for the event, and these were meant to guide its outcomes. Participants were also expected to consider India's role in the field.

Beyond the summit itself, the event was placed within a longer series of international meetings on AI. Earlier summits had addressed the promises and risks of the technology, and their discussions often returned to questions of human intent, safety and accountability. The India gathering was presented as a continuation of that conversation, with a stronger emphasis on development and on the needs of countries in the Global South.

questions.q: Where was the India AI Impact Summit 2026 held?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the summit was held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

questions.q: Which city will host the 2027 World Summit on Artificial Intelligence?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Switzerland will host the 2027 World Summit on AI in Geneva.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The India AI Impact Summit 2026 set out four key objectives.
Reason (R): One of its objectives is to promote responsible and ethical AI, addressing algorithmic bias, privacy protection and accountability.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason describes one objective and does not explain why the summit set out four objectives.

questions.q: How many Chakras (Priority Cooperation Areas) were identified for the summit?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists seven Chakras (Priority Cooperation Areas) for the summit.

questions.q:
Read the following statements about the summit:
I. The summit was described as the first multilateral AI summit in the Global South.
II. Its theme was 'Sarvajana Hitaya, Sarvajana Sukhaya'.
III. It was the first multilateral AI summit held in Europe.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III wrongly places the summit in Europe.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the summit are correct?
I. The summit set out four key objectives.
II. One of its objectives addresses algorithmic bias and privacy protection.
III. The 'Planet' Sutra stands for Ethical Innovation.
IV. Switzerland will host the 2027 World Summit on AI in Paris.
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct, while IV wrongly names Paris instead of Geneva.

questions.q: Which of the summit's objectives involves cooperation between governments, startups, academia and industry?
options: Translating global AI discussions into development outcomes
Positioning India as a Global AI Hub
Building partnerships between governments, startups, academia and industry
questions.explanation: Objective 3 is to build partnerships between governments, startups, academia and industry.

quizzes.title: Summit Theme and Objectives: TITA practice
quizzes.passage:
A major artificial intelligence meeting was held in India in 2026, and its organisers presented it as a new chapter for the field. Earlier discussions were described as following a Western safety-first model. The organisers argued for a different starting point, one in which development is central and AI is judged by how far it improves the lives of ordinary citizens. This framing placed the meeting within a longer series of international AI gatherings that had come before it.

The meeting was built around a short guiding phrase that pointed to the welfare of everyone. A set of guiding principles shaped its agenda, covering inclusive development, ethical innovation and sustainable societal impact. Within this framework, the meeting identified priority areas where cooperation could produce results, including health, farming and education.

The meeting was also meant to promote the responsible development of AI. Beyond the gathering itself, the organisers hoped to link its outcomes with national programmes for digital growth and with a growing domestic technology base. Its discussions were expected to move from broad global conversations towards practical applications that can be scaled across a large country.

Some participants were expected to focus on how India's own research institutions and companies could contribute to this work, and the wider aim was to strengthen an indigenous ecosystem for the technology.

questions.q: In which city is Bharat Mandapam, the venue of the India AI Impact Summit 2026? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet places Bharat Mandapam, the summit venue, in New Delhi.

questions.q: Which city will host the 2027 World Summit on Artificial Intelligence? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 2027 World Summit on AI will be hosted in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: What is the name of the first of the three Sutras? (one word)
questions.explanation: The first Sutra is People, which stands for Inclusive Development.

questions.q: Under which objective number of the summit are algorithmic bias and privacy protection addressed? (number)
questions.explanation: Objective 2 promotes responsible and ethical AI and addresses algorithmic bias, privacy and accountability.

questions.q: How many Sutras (guiding principles) does the summit have? (number)
questions.explanation: The summit's guiding principles are the three Sutras: People, Planet and Progress.

questions.q: What is the name of the paradigm that puts development outcomes ahead of safety? (one or two words)
questions.explanation: The summit signalled a shift from a Western safety-first model to an impact-first developmental paradigm.

questions.q: Which priority area is the sixth of the seven Chakras? (name)
questions.explanation: The seven Chakras run Healthcare, Agriculture, Education, Governance, Climate action, Digital Economy and Social Inclusion, so the sixth is Digital Economy.

quizzes.title: Previous Summits and M.A.N.A.V.: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage:
The framework that India presented at its 2026 AI summit was described as human-centric and aimed at ethical and inclusive artificial intelligence. Its principles were arranged so that each letter of the framework's name stands for one idea. The principles were presented together as a single design. The framework reflects concerns that have appeared in earlier international meetings on the subject, where the balance between innovation and safety has been a recurring theme. The framework was unveiled by the Prime Minister during the summit.

Earlier summits form part of the background to this work. A series of such meetings has been held in different countries, and the first of them was focused on risks from advanced systems. Later gatherings followed in other years and places. Taken as a whole, the series of meetings shows how the subject has been discussed over several years.

The principles in the framework touch on several themes, including the need for systems to be fair and transparent, the importance of clear responsibility in governance, and the value of strengthening domestic capacity. They also address the spread of false content online. Taken together, these ideas show how the framework tries to connect technology with public purpose. These themes are presented as part of a human-centric approach.

questions.q: Which country hosted the 1st AI Safety Summit, where the Bletchley Declaration was adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the UK hosted the 1st AI Safety Summit and adopted the Bletchley Declaration.

questions.q: In which year was the 3rd AI Action Summit held?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the 3rd AI Action Summit as held in 2025 in Paris, France.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 'V' principle of the M.A.N.A.V. framework requires AI systems to ensure trust, safety and legal compliance.
Reason (R): Sovereign AI refers to a nation's autonomous capability to develop, control and deploy its own AI technologies.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason defines Sovereign AI and does not explain the 'V' principle.

questions.q: Which principle of the M.A.N.A.V. framework aims to bridge the digital divide and reach marginalised populations?
questions.explanation: The second 'A' stands for Accessible and Inclusive AI, which aims to bridge the digital divide and reach marginalised populations.

questions.q:
Read the following statements about the M.A.N.A.V. framework:
I. The 'M' principle stands for Moral and Ethical Systems, requiring AI to be fair and transparent.
II. The 'N' principle stands for National Sovereignty and includes securing critical datasets.
III. The 'M' principle requires AI to operate without any human oversight.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the 'M' principle makes AI subject to human oversight.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about earlier and current AI summits are correct?
I. The M.A.N.A.V. framework was unveiled by the Prime Minister at the summit.
II. The AI Seoul Summit took place in 2024.
III. The AI Seoul Summit was hosted solely by France.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the Seoul Summit was co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the UK government.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Bletchley Declaration   ->   A. Held in Paris, France
II. AI Seoul Summit   ->   B. Trust, safety and legal compliance
III. 3rd AI Action Summit   ->   C. Co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the UK government
IV. 'V' of M.A.N.A.V.   ->   D. Aligning AI with human intent, safeguarding rights
questions.explanation: Bletchley aligns AI with human intent, Seoul was co-hosted by Korea and the UK, the 3rd AI Action Summit was in Paris, and 'V' covers trust, safety and legal compliance.

quizzes.title: Previous Summits and M.A.N.A.V.: TITA practice
quizzes.passage:
India's 2026 summit saw the unveiling of a human-centric framework for ethical and inclusive artificial intelligence. The framework is built on a set of principles, each represented by one letter of its name. Its principles address several concerns, including the design of AI systems, the responsibility of institutions, the role of domestic capacity and data, and the role of trust in an era of misinformation.

The framework was introduced against a background of earlier international meetings on AI, held in several countries. The series began with a meeting focused on the risks linked to advanced AI systems. Later summits followed in other years and cities, and the subject has remained on the international agenda.

Each principle in the framework is meant to be read alongside the others, and together they form one human-centric approach. The framework therefore links technical design with questions of governance, legitimacy and public trust. Its ideas were presented as part of a wider effort to make AI serve people.

Several earlier meetings addressed similar questions from different angles, and the summit's framework was placed within that wider international context. The subject has been discussed in forums across different countries, and the India gathering was one more step in that conversation. Its framework formed part of that wider debate.

questions.explanation: The booklet states the UK hosted the 1st AI Safety Summit.

questions.q: In which city was the 3rd AI Action Summit held? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the 3rd AI Action Summit in Paris, France, in 2025.

questions.q: Which letter of the M.A.N.A.V. framework stands for National Sovereignty? (one letter)
questions.explanation: The third letter, N, stands for National Sovereignty.

questions.q: In which year was the AI Seoul Summit held? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the AI Seoul Summit took place in 2024.

questions.q: What is the name of the principle represented by the second 'A' of M.A.N.A.V.? (name)
questions.explanation: The second A stands for Accessible and Inclusive AI.

questions.q: What does the 'M' of M.A.N.A.V. stand for? (two words)

questions.q: Which declaration was adopted at the UK-hosted AI Safety Summit? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UK's 1st AI Safety Summit adopted the Bletchley Declaration.

quizzes.title: Sovereign Models and Platforms: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage:
India's push for sovereign artificial intelligence has produced a range of models and platforms, some built for general language tasks and others for specific sectors. The idea behind sovereign AI is that a country should be able to develop, control and deploy its own AI technologies. Several domestic firms and research bodies are working on such models, and their work has been presented as part of the national effort.

Language is a central concern in this work. Indian languages are numerous, and systems that handle them require careful development. Some of the national efforts focus on translation and speech, so that people can use digital services in their own languages. Others concentrate on text generation, aiming to produce fluent output that reads naturally to users. Such work must also reflect the cultural contexts of different communities.

Health is another major area. Platforms in this field are intended to test AI systems on real-world data while protecting privacy. Some of them are linked to government health missions that aim to help their use spread across the country.

Biotechnology is also part of the picture. Policies that connect AI with life sciences aim to bring computer models and laboratory work closer together. Such efforts are presented as a way to link research with national priorities.

questions.q: Which institute developed the BODH platform in collaboration with the National Health Authority?
questions.explanation: The booklet says BODH was developed by IIT Kanpur in collaboration with the National Health Authority.

questions.q: Which company developed the Vachana text-to-speech model?
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies Vachana as a text-to-speech model by Gnani.ai.

questions.q: What does the word 'Mulankur', used in the Bio-AI Mulankur Hubs, mean in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Mulankur means 'Seed' or 'Foundation' in Sanskrit.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B are large language models capable of generating human-like text.
Reason (R): Vikram is a multilingual chatbot that enables seamless conversations across Indian languages.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason describes a different model and does not explain the first.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. BODH   ->   A. National framework for responsible AI integration in healthcare
II. SAHI   ->   B. Privacy-preserving benchmarking platform for health AI
III. VoicERA   ->   C. Integrates AI with biotechnology under the BioE3 policy
IV. Bio-AI Mulankur Hubs   ->   D. Open-source, end-to-end voice AI stack
questions.explanation: BODH is a privacy-preserving benchmarking platform, SAHI is a national healthcare framework, VoicERA is an open-source voice stack, and Mulankur Hubs integrate AI with biotechnology.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's sovereign AI models and platforms:
I. Vachana is a text-to-speech model that supports 12 Indian languages.
II. Param2 17B is a multilingual foundational AI model developed by Sarvam AI.
III. VoicERA was developed by the Digital India BHASHINI Division.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because Param2 17B was developed by BharatGen.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about India's platforms are correct?
I. BHASHINI is an AI-powered national language translation and speech platform.
II. The Bio-AI Mulankur Hubs aim to have laboratory experiments validate AI predictions in real time.
III. Sarvam's Vikram is a text-to-speech model.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because Vikram is a multilingual chatbot.

quizzes.title: Sovereign Models and Platforms: TITA practice
quizzes.passage:
Sovereign artificial intelligence refers to a country's ability to develop, control and deploy its own AI technologies, and India has pursued this goal through a number of models and platforms. Some are designed for language, others for sectors such as health and biotechnology. The work is carried out by private companies, research institutions and public bodies, which together form a national effort.

Indian languages present a particular challenge for developers. The country has many languages, and a model that works well in one may perform less well in another. Some platforms therefore concentrate on speech and translation, helping citizens use digital services in their own language. Other efforts focus on generating written text in a fluent and natural form.

In health, platforms are being built to test AI systems against real-world data while protecting patient privacy. National frameworks also set out how AI may be integrated into healthcare services. Several of these initiatives sit within existing government missions.

Biotechnology forms another part of the picture. Policies that connect AI with the life sciences aim to bring computer models and laboratory work closer together, so that predictions can be checked by experiments. Such efforts are presented as a way to link research with national priorities.

questions.q: Which organisation developed the Param2 17B multilingual foundational AI model? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies Param2 17B as a multilingual foundational AI model by BharatGen.

questions.q: Under which policy is the Bio-AI Mulankur Hubs initiative placed? (policy acronym)
questions.explanation: The Mulankur Hubs integrate AI with biotechnology under the BioE3 policy.

questions.q: How many Indian languages does the Vachana text-to-speech model support? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Vachana supports 12 Indian languages.

questions.q: Under which ministry does the Digital India BHASHINI Division operate? (abbreviation)
accept: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.explanation: The Digital India BHASHINI Division operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).

questions.q: Which institute developed BODH in collaboration with the National Health Authority? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says BODH was developed by IIT Kanpur in collaboration with the National Health Authority.

questions.q: What is the name of the open-source, end-to-end voice AI stack? (name)
questions.explanation: VoicERA is described as an open-source, end-to-end voice AI stack.

questions.q: What is the name of Sarvam AI's multilingual chatbot? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Sarvam's Vikram as a multilingual chatbot.
